title: Vegetative Growth and Rhizome Expansion Characteristics of Wild Poa pratensis L. from Gansu Province Under Drought Stress
content: Poa pratensis L. is a perennial rhizomatous cool season turfgrass with great application potential for turf establishment and degraded grassland restoration in arid regions. This study aimed to reveal the response patterns of above ground vegetative growth and rhizome expansion under drought stress, and to clarify the regulatory mechanisms mediated by endogenous hormones. A pot water controlled experiment was conducted using 11 wild Poa pratensis L. accessions collected from Gansu Province and the commercial cultivar Midnight (as control). Four soil water gradients were set, corresponding to 75%-85%, 55%-65%, 35%-45%, and 15%-25% of field capacity. Above ground morphological traits, rhizome expansion traits, and endogenous hormone contents (JA, IAA, GA, CTK and ABA) in leaves were measured. Spearman correlation analysis was used to decipher the synergistic and trade off relationships among phenotypic traits, as well as the associations between endogenous hormones and phenotypic indices. The results showed that: (1) Drought significantly inhibited above ground vegetative growth including plant height, leaf length, leaf width and tiller number. Most above ground traits were sensitive to water deficit. The Yuzhong (YZ) accession exhibited the weakest growth inhibition, while the Tianzhu (TZ) and Anding (AD) accessions suffered the most severe suppression. (2) Rhizome traits differed significantly among accessions. The Lingtai (LT), Yuzhong (YZ), Qinzhou (QZ) and Weiyuan (WY) accessions adapted to drought via rhizome proliferation, thickening and volume accumulation; by contrast, rhizome architecture of the Xihe (XH) accession was markedly restricted by drought. (3) Drought induced divergent responses of endogenous hormones. The contents of ABA and JA continuously increased with drought intensification, whereas CTK, GA and IAA gradually decreased. The overall hormone levels of YZ remained relatively stable, and XH showed an intense response to drought. (4) Correlation analysis indicated that Yuzhong, Lingtai and Qinzhou are elite drought resistant accessions with coordinated maintenance of vegetative growth, rhizome expansion and endogenous hormones. Collectively, these findings provide a theoretical basis for the breeding of new drought-tolerant turfgrass cultivars in Northwest China.
